newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Pol Pot said to be in northern Cambodian jungle.
newsitem.headline: Pol Pot said to be in northern Cambodian jungle.

text.p: Reviled Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot is in the jungle east of Anlong Veng after fleeing his northern stronghold with at least three top officials as hostages, a senior Cambodian military official told reporters on Saturday.

Deputy chief of general staff Nhiek Bun Chhay produced a photograph that he said showed the dead bodies of Khmer Rouge defence chief Son Sen, his wife Yun Yat and other family members said to have been murdered by Pol Pot this week.

He said Pol Pot was holed up approximately 20 km (12 miles) east of Anlong Veng in rough jungle terrain with 250 to 300 fighters and their families. He was holding right-hand man Nuon Chea, the Khmer Rouge's nominal leader Khieu Samphan and northern commander Ta Mok as hostages.
"In the few days ahead, first, Pol Pot can lay down his arms. Second, Pol Pot can kill all of his leaders and then kill himself," Nhiek Bun Chhay said at a press conference.
He said 1,000 rebel troops from five divisions have broken with Pol Pot and are surrounding him, and added that Thailand had sealed its border and was cooperating with Cambodian authorities.
The Khmer Rouge has been blamed for the deaths of more than one million people through starvations, disease, overwork or executions during their 1975-79 rule of Cambodia.
